content.comment_body: Hello, We are currently testing new features in [product_name] [version_no]. Our main goal is to remotely access these units via an ADSL connection. I have set up a unit at home, assigned it the IP 192.168.0.20, and can access it within my local network. Port 102 is forwarded in my router to this device. My ADSL uses a static IP. From the office, I have tried to connect to my home IP using [product_name] and provided the gateway information from our network, but connection fails. Has anyone succeeded in establishing this kind of remote access? Thank you.
It may be necessary to enter your router's IP address as the gateway in your [product_name] configuration.
Thank you for your suggestion. The device's IP, subnet, and gateway are all configured according to the local network settings. Thanks.
Hello, Try forwarding Port 10001, as that is the port used by [product_name][version_no]. Hope this helps.
Thank you, I will test this solution.

Thank you for all the advice. We have established remote connectivity to the device. However, does anyone know how to connect to multiple devices within the same network? Is it possible to assign different ports, for example setting one device to 10001 and another to 10002, and manage port forwarding for each individually? Thanks.

analysis.insight_summary: The user was unable to establish remote access to a [product_name] [version_no] using [product_name] software. Network port configuration and router settings were the main issues. With forum advice, the user forwarded the correct port and succeeded in remote connectivity, but now seeks solutions for connecting and managing multiple devices on the same network, preferably through flexible port assignments.
analysis.user_expectations: The user desires straightforward remote access over the internet to one or more [product_name] devices, along with the capability to assign different ports for managing multiple devices on a single network.
